title: How do we split a number into thousands, hundreds, tens and ones?
description: Joseph reads two readings on his uncle's bus in Kochi. The video splits each reading into thousands, hundreds, tens and ones.
teaching_notes: One idea: each digit tells how many of its place, and a zero holds its place. Watch for the child who drops the zero.

source: Write 1,380 and 9,123 as thousands, hundreds, tens and ones.
video_script.why: The child reads small numbers by place but has not split a four-digit number into all its places.
video_script.substitution: Read the digits from the left, one place at a time, and keep the zero as a place holder.
video_script.anchor: the kilometre dial of Joseph's uncle's bus in Kochi
video_script.wrong_move: Chintu thinks a zero is nothing, so he drops it. The zero holds the ones place; without it the other digits slide into the wrong places.
video_script.payoff_line: the zero keeps the other digits in their places

final_answer.value: 1,380 = 1 Thousand + 3 Hundreds + 8 Tens + 0 Ones, and 9,123 = 9 Thousands + 1 Hundred + 2 Tens + 3 Ones
final_answer.spoken: one thousand, three hundreds, eight tens and nought ones, and nine thousands, one hundred, two tens and three ones

never_show: the your-turn answer 5 Thousands + 2 Hundreds + 0 Tens + 6 Ones
maths_rules: warm-up number: 2,456 = 2 Thousands, 4 Hundreds, 5 Tens, 6 Ones
slip: dropping the 0 of 1,380 gives 138, so the digits shift to the wrong places
your turn: 5,206 = 5 Thousands + 2 Hundreds + 0 Tens + 6 Ones; never shown
video_script.design: One idea: split a number by place, left to right. Wrong idea: the zero is nothing and can be dropped. The bus dial stays as the anchor; the place chart builds on the stage.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='bus'/>Joseph's uncle drives a bus in Kochi.
<bookmark mark='two'/>One dial reads one thousand three hundred eighty. Another reads nine thousand one hundred twenty three.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Write each reading as thousands, hundreds, tens and ones.

beats.on_screen: the anchor holds still and gets an accent underline

marks.stop: the anchor is underlined in the accent colour

narration: <bookmark mark='stop'/>Stop the video. Say your answer out loud.

beats.on_screen: a place chart with columns Th, H, T and O; the warm-up number 2,456 drops in digit by digit from the left

marks.cols: the four columns light up from the left
marks.each: each digit of the warm-up number drops into its column
marks.say: the chart reads 2 Thousands, 4 Hundreds, 5 Tens, 6 Ones

narration: <bookmark mark='cols'/>Read a number from the left, one place at a time.
<bookmark mark='each'/>Take two thousand four hundred fifty six.
<bookmark mark='say'/>It has two thousands, four hundreds, five tens and six ones.
<bookmark mark='digit'/>Each digit tells how many of its place.

beats.on_screen: Chintu's bubble shows 1,380 with the 0 crossed out; the digits 1, 3, 8 slide right and the ones box is left empty; the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

marks.chintu: Chintu's bubble appears with the zero crossed out
marks.slide: the digits slide one place to the right
marks.strike: the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='chintu'/>A zero is nothing, so I leave out the zero. One thousand, three hundreds, eight.
<bookmark mark='slide'/>Without the zero, every digit slides one place to the right.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>Then eight tens would turn into eight ones.

beats.on_screen: the first dial reading fills the chart: Th 1, H 3, T 8, O 0; below it 1,000 + 300 + 80 + 0

marks.one: the digits 1, 3, 8, 0 drop into the chart
marks.say: the line 1 Thousand, 3 Hundreds, 8 Tens, 0 Ones appears
marks.pay: the zero glows in the ones column

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>The first reading has the digits one, three, eight and nought.
<bookmark mark='say'/>That is one thousand, three hundreds, eight tens and nought ones.
<bookmark mark='pay'/>The nought is not left out, because the zero keeps the other digits in their places.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Add them back, one thousand, three hundred and eighty, and we get the reading again.

beats.on_screen: the second reading fills a new chart: Th 9, H 1, T 2, O 3; below it 9,000 + 100 + 20 + 3

marks.nine: the digits 9, 1, 2, 3 drop into the chart
marks.say: the line 9 Thousands, 1 Hundred, 2 Tens, 3 Ones appears

narration: <bookmark mark='nine'/>Do the same for the second reading.
<bookmark mark='say'/>It is nine thousands, one hundred, two tens and three ones.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Add them back, nine thousand, one hundred, twenty and three, and we get the reading again.

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Read a number from the left, one place at a time.
<bookmark mark='two'/>A zero holds its place, so never leave it out.
